newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebel chief's mother, sister kidnapped in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Rebel chief's mother, sister kidnapped in Colombia.

text.p: A right-wing paramilitary group claimed responsibility on Thursday for kidnapping the mother and sister of one of Colombia's top leftist guerrilla leaders.

A statement from the so-called "Peasant Self-Defence" group -- a shadowy organisation operating out of the northwest banana-growing region of Uraba and neighbouring Cordoba province -- said the kidnappings were to press for the release of all hostages held by rebels of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).
It did not elaborate but the FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest rebel group, specialises in kidnapping and the protection of rural drug operations.
The mother and sister of Luciano Arango Marin, a FARC chieftain popularly known as Ivan Marquez, were abducted late on Wednesday from their home in Neiva, the capital of southwest Huila province.
A police spokesman said the kidnapping was carried out by a group of about six gunmen who identified themselves as agents of the prosecutor-general's office.
At least three other family members of senior FARC rebels have been kidnapped since July.
